positive.excerpt: The government's new carbon tax will add just £1.50 a week to the average household's energy bill, a small price to pay for securing a greener future for our children. Critics argue the policy doesn't go far enough, but ministers insist the gradual increase will be barely noticeable in family budgets.
positive.mechanism: Per-week framing used to minimize a cost ('just £1.50 a week') without stating the annual or lifetime total

positive.excerpt: Health officials today announced a decade-long plan to reduce sugar consumption, cutting just 5% from the national diet each year. The incremental approach means families won't feel the pinch at the checkout, while still reaping long-term benefits for public health.
positive.mechanism: 'Only a small reduction over a decade' applied to a cost without lump-sum equivalent stated

positive.excerpt: The stadium's $1.2 billion renovation will cost taxpayers just $20 per year over the next 30 years, city officials announced today. 'That's less than the price of a single game ticket,' said the mayor, emphasizing how affordable the project will be for local residents.
positive.mechanism: Long amortization period cited to shrink apparent size of total cost ('$20 per year over 30 years')

near_miss.excerpt: The new highway project will cost $500 million, or about $100 per resident when spread across the state's five million taxpayers. Officials note this is comparable to the cost of a monthly gym membership for each household.
near_miss.why_not: The lump-sum total is stated alongside the diffuse framing, preventing asymmetric comparison.

near_miss.excerpt: Doctors recommend patients take a 10mg daily dose of the medication, which works out to just $30 per month. The treatment's benefits are immediate, with most patients reporting symptom relief within days.
near_miss.why_not: The cost and benefit are both presented in near-term frames, maintaining temporal symmetry.

contrast.excerpt: Despite mounting evidence that the light rail project is over budget and behind schedule, city councilors voted to allocate another $200 million today. 'We've already invested too much to turn back now,' said the transportation commissioner, citing the $800 million spent to date.
contrast.distinction: Focuses on past investments already made (sunk costs) rather than reframing future costs in diffuse temporal terms.
